title: The journey begins
summary: The pilgrim says farewell and sets off for the Heart of the Dark.

title: Planning the route
summary: Sets how many road events the journey has: two from near the Drakwald, three from further away, four from the far corners of the world. Distance is measured from Marienburg (province 222), at the edge of the forest.

calls: brayherd.10; brayherd.11; brayherd.12; brayherd.13; brayherd.15; brayherd.20; brayherd.4
title: Road event roll
summary: Picks one road event the pilgrim has not had yet. When the road events are used up, or none fits, the pilgrim reaches the Heart of the Dark (brayherd.4).

title: The Heart of the Dark
summary: The pilgrim arrives. Two events at the Heart of the Dark follow.

title: Smoke over the trees
summary: The warband stumbles on a human hamlet in the forest. Burn it, drag the survivors to the Herdstone as sacrifices (pleases the Herdstone most), or leave it and keep the pace.

title: A challenger in the warband
summary: A young gor of the pilgrim's own warband challenges for the leadership, as beastmen do. Fight him (better odds with martial skill, duelists and the brave), let the bestigors kill him (costs prestige), or, for the cunning, send him to lead a raid that goes wrong.

title: The Dark Omen
summary: Malagor, the crow-winged bray-shaman, reads the pilgrim's fate. Letting him read the entrails gives a good or ill omen (beastmen_blood_omen or beastmen_ill_omen); a sacrifice buys better odds; driving him off angers the Herdstone.

title: The Brass Bull
summary: Taurox, the Doombull of brass flesh, crashes past on an endless rampage. Join it (glory, wounds or worse; pleases the Herdstone), steer the minotaurs at a human town (cunning pilgrims), or get out of the way.

title: A warlord's invitation
summary: An AI beastman king or emperor (a rival if there is one) invites the pilgrim to his camp. Accept (brayherd.16), use it to murder a rival (schemers, brayherd.18) or keep to your own tent.

title: The warlord's feast
summary: Usually a good rest. A host who is not yet a friend may become one; a rival host may poison the pilgrim (eight times likelier if deceitful): half the time that kills, half the time it ends in brayherd.17.

title: Waking in a ditch
summary: The poisoned pilgrim survives with food poisoning (or poisoned, without Reapers) and a warning to stay away.

title: Fatal hospitality
summary: A schemer's murder attempt on the rival host: a clean kill and escape (more likely with high intrigue), a kill that costs the pilgrim's life, or a failure that does. Pilgrims who cannot die carry on with the journey.

title: Tracks of a Jabberslythe
summary: The pilgrim finds the work of a great Jabberslythe and can hunt it (brayherd.21). Hunters always do.

title: How the hunt goes
summary: Even odds: the pilgrim corners the beast (brayherd.23), meets a rival hunter (brayherd.22) or gets lost (brayherd.24).

title: The other hunter
summary: A lone bestigor hunts the same beast. Take him into your court (better odds at the kill), leave him be, or treat him as a rival (worse odds, and the pilgrim grows cruel and paranoid).

title: The Jabberslythe cornered
summary: Fighting gives prestige and a roll: mastery of the hunt, a wound, the beast escaping, maiming or death. A hunting companion makes mastery likelier, a slain rival maiming and death. Fleeing costs prestige and courage.

title: Lost in the forest
summary: The pilgrim wanders lost for weeks: may fall ill (if healthy), and may become stressed, depressed or wroth.

title: Heart of the Dark event roll
summary: Picks one event the pilgrim has not had yet at the Heart of the Dark. When they are used up, or none fits, the rite at the Herdstone follows (brayherd.39).

title: The fighting ring
summary: Bestigors brawl in a ring. Duelists win money and pride; others can try their luck. Fighting pleases the Herdstone; watching and betting does not.

title: The shrine of a single god
summary: Bestigors worship one Chaos god at a defiled altar. Joining in may make the pilgrim cynical or turn them to that god; an undivided pilgrim can denounce them (piety, but the Herdstone frowns); or study their symbols.

title: The herd market
summary: A market of meat, slaves and plunder. Feast (may turn gluttonous), buy a beastman artifact, or steal one (intrigue 15 or elusive shadow).

title: Before the Great Herdstone
summary: Ends the pilgrimage. The rite's outcome is rolled from the favour gathered on the journey plus half the pilgrim's diplomacy, rank and the Brayherd's opinion: a bad rite (favour 100 for those who humble themselves, at a cost in prestige), an okay one (favour 150) or a great one (favour 300, piety, martial and health).

title: A bray shaman for the court
summary: Boon: the Brayherd's governor sends a bray shaman (wizard, often marked by a god or a mutation) to serve as court physician. Stronger while the Brayherd is united. Announced by brayherd.51.

title: The bray shaman arrives
summary: Letter from the governor; the shaman becomes court physician.

title: A war leader for the court
summary: Boon: the governor sends a scarred bestigor of the ruler's god to lead the armies (strategist modifier, commander if a slot is free). Announced by brayherd.53.

title: The war leader arrives
summary: Letter from the governor; the bestigor becomes a commander if possible.

title: A daemonic artifact
summary: Boon: a random beastman artifact the ruler does not own yet.

title: A gift of Chaos
summary: Boon: a mutation (hides, runes, tusks, senses, limbs) or a bigger set of horns, up to a crown of horns. About one roll in six brings nothing visible. Every roll counts towards the mutation counter.

title: A request for a bray
summary: Boon: the governor picks a bride for a male ruler or relative, either from his own bloodline or a lowborn beauty, and gives her family, looks and a personality (abler while the Brayherd is united). Then brayherd.61. The decision only allows male grooms, so the bride is always created. FROMFROMFROM the groom.

title: The bride is on her way
summary: Letter to the ruler who asked; the bride arrives in two to three weeks.

title: The bride arrives
summary: The bride and groom can marry again; the wedding follows (brayherd.63).

title: A ruinous union
summary: The groom takes the bride as consort: prestige (more if she is of the Brayherd's own blood) and, for a ruler who married himself, five years of peace with the Brayherd. Tells the ruler who asked (brayherd.64).

title: The wedding is announced
